title: Tighter coils, more curvature
hook: Which coil bends the cord more gently?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: A circle’s curvature is the reciprocal of its radius. A larger-radius loop uses more length per turn and bends less sharply; neither the cord material nor total length changes.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

recall.question: You coil a cord in loops of 15 cm radius instead of 30 cm. What happens to its curvature?
options: It stays the same: same cord
recall.why: Curvature = 1 ÷ radius. Half the radius gives twice the curvature, a sharper bend, and each turn uses less cord. The card gives no product-specific bend limit.
